properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 2 at 7:21AM MST until November 5 at 11:45PM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
...The Flood Watch continues for the following rivers in Colorado...

Rio Grande At Alamosa affecting Alamosa Vicinity/Central San Luis
Valley.

For the Rio Grande...including Alamosa...flooding is forecasted to
begin by mid week.

* WHAT...Flooding is possible.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Alamosa.

* WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon to Thursday evening.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:30 AM MST Monday the stage was 3.0 feet.
- Forecast...Flood stage may be reached early Wednesday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
If you are in the watch area, remain alert to possible flooding.

Residents and those with interests near the river should monitor
rising water levels and be prepared for possible Flood Warnings.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 330 PM MST.

* WHEN...Through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 2 at 12:54AM MST until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of north central, northwest, and west central New
Mexico, including the following areas, in north central New Mexico,
Far Northwest Highlands, Jemez Mountains, Northwest Highlands and
Tusas Mountains Including Chama. In northwest New Mexico, Chuska
Mountains and Northwest Plateau. In west central New Mexico, San
Francisco River Valley, Southwest Mountains, West Central
Highlands, West Central Mountains and West Central Plateau.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM MST this morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Another round of widespread rainfall continues this morning with
total rainfall amounts generally between 1 and 2 inches near and
west of the Continental Divide, except near 3 inches in favored
upslope regions of the Tusas Mountains near Chama and in the
Chuska Mountains. This rainfall is occurring over very saturated
soils which will increase runoff. River flooding may continue
into Tuesday.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Collier County; Inland Collier County; Mainland Monroe
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 1 at 11:59PM EST until November 2 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
An upper level low will will continue to influence storms in the
Gulf and Bahamas through Monday. With the lack of a strong synoptic
surface forcing mechanism, predictability as to where and when heavy
rain will fall remains low. However, the environment continues to
support the potential for heavy rainfall and slow moving cells.

* WHAT...Heavy rain may cause, or worsen ongoing urban and street
flooding.

* WHERE...All of South Florida

* WHEN...Through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Isolated to scattered areas of flash flooding will be
possible, with the main impact being street flooding, road
closures, and limited impact to structures in flood prone areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Pockets of very heavy rainfall resulted in localized flash
flooding on Sunday and those areas, and others, have the
potential to be impacted again on Monday. Forecast amounts look
very similar to yesterday, with common amounts of 1 to 3 inches
where showers and storms occur. Scattered locations around south
Florida may see closer to 3 to 5 inches of rain. The more
isolated high end amounts have the potential to peak around 6 to
9 inches. These amounts could accumulate rather quickly, on the
order of 2 to 4 hours.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.
